name: China economy
summary: China's new home prices fell 2.4% on a year in October, a 40th straight annual fall; the property slump persists
state: New home prices across 70 Chinese cities fell 2.4% year on year in October after 2.8% in September, the 40th consecutive annual decline though the smallest since November 2025, and slipped 0.1% on the month (Trading Economics, 16 Nov). The South China Morning Post reports that Beijing's latest property stimulus is falling short in lower-tier cities. The prolonged property slump keeps Watch; no hard landing below 3% growth, financial contagion or sharp capital-control tightening was found as of 26 Nov.
for_you: A weak Chinese property market holds down demand for steel, copper and other commodities, and for goods sold into China.
rubric_hit: Renewed property slump (home prices falling 40 months) = Watch; growth not below 3%

sources.title: Trading Economics — China new home prices fall the least in 11 months
South China Morning Post — Beijing's latest property stimulus falls short in lower-tier cities

why: China is the world's factory and the biggest marginal buyer of commodities; a hard landing would ripple through every supply chain.
drivers: Property sector, local-government debt, exports and tariffs, deflation, stimulus.

rubric.alert: Hard landing (growth < 3%), financial contagion, or capital controls tightened sharply.
rubric.watch: Deflation, renewed property-developer defaults, or growth clearly below target.
rubric.normal: Growth near official target, stable property sales, no financial contagion.
